ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed shareholders, UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and the Egyptian FIU/Government terrorist designation list. PEP status must be identified during KYC, classified by risk rating, and subjected to enhanced due diligence with senior compliance officer approval. Screening evidence must be retained for at least five years after filing and refreshed before activation of any payment rail.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI e-Services Portal — Company Name Reservation Service operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be rendered in Arabic script. For foreign-invested LLCs, a Latin-character transliteration or English translation is accepted as a registered auxiliary name, provided the Arabic name is the controlling version in Arabic-language filings and commercial registry documents. All transliterations must follow standard phonemic transcription to avoid conflict with existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with GAFI's Investor Services and Dispute Resolution Department within 15 business days of the rejection notice. GAFI must render a decision on the appeal within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file a judicial review application before the State Council Administrative Court within 60 days. In parallel, the applicant may immediately submit a new name reservation request with a modified corporate identifier to avoid delay. Name reservation extensions may be requested before expiry; extensions are discretionary and subject to GAFI approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permissible as the statutory registered office of the Egyptian LLC. A physical Egyptian office address is mandatory for the ODC. A virtual office may be used only for ancillary correspondence, and must not be presented as the GAFI registered office or payroll/substance location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% baseline annual probability for a standard ODC with a physical office and payroll substance; likelihood rises to 30% if GAFI investment incentives are claimed or if the tax authority conducts employment substance audits during the first fiscal year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, Articles 20-27 (Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 3, 18, 21; Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2316 of 2017 (Executive Regulations of Investment Law)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department and One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry (Al-Shahr Al-Ti dari)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd Ta'sis) together with GAFI electronic incorporation application and Commercial Registration Form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EGP 50,000 minimum paid-up capital for LLC under Companies Law No. 159/1981; capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account with a licensed Egyptian bank and confirmed by bank certificate prior to registration; no public share subscription is permitted
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders approve the formation of the Company as a Limited Liability Company governed by the Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association are approved and shall be filed with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones; that the registered office is established and fixed at the address specified in the Articles; that all issued shares are subscribed and the minimum capital deposit is authorized; that the first directors are appointed; that the Chairman and Managing Director are authorized to sign the incorporation documents, open bank accounts, appoint the auditor, affix the corporate seal, and complete the statutory registration formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name approval and reservation with GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services One-Stop Shop, Headquarters, Cairo (or online through GAFI Digital Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation application through the GAFI investor portal or in person, selecting up to three alternative names; GAFI verifies uniqueness, non-confusing similarity, and compliance with public order and good morals; once approved, the name is reserved for 60 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation application form
Passport or national ID copy of each founder
Power of attorney for the incorporator, if applicable
Statement of intended business activity (software development and maintenance, ISIC 6202 / NAICS 541512)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a written objection to the GAFI Registration Committee within 30 days of refusal; propose alternative name variants; if the conflict persists, seek an administrative review by GAFI's Dispute Resolution Committee and amend the name list accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office under the Egyptian Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bilingual Arabic-English Memorandum and Articles of Association, circulate the document to all founding members, collect signatures, and have the document notarized before the competent Egyptian notary public; for foreign founders, passport copies and apostilled powers of attorney or board resolutions must be attached.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
English certified translation of the draft (if original is not Arabic)
GAFI name approval certificate
Passport or national ID copies of founding members
Lease contract or title deed evidencing the intended registered office address
Statutory declaration that shares are subscribed by each member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify the corrections indicated by the notary and re-submit the amended document for same-day notarization; if refusal is based on missing document, submit the missing item by courier and request expedited review; if notary error is identified, apply to the Ministry of Justice Notary Department for correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of provisional bank account and deposit of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g., Commercial International Bank, National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account using the draft notarized incorporation documents; deposit the minimum paid-up capital (EGP 50,000 or such greater amount stated in the Articles) into a blocked account; obtain a capital deposit certificate issued by the bank, sealed with the bank's authorized signature, for submission to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Provisional authenticated Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name approval certificate
Passport or national ID copies of all signatories
Power of attorney or corporate resolution for foreign corporate founders
Proof of legal address of the company
Bank account application and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC or beneficial ownership data, provide corrected declarations and certified translation of the company documents; if approval is delayed beyond 10 business days, close the application and reapply at another licensed bank; maintain a copy of the formal bank refusal for GAFI escalation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of GAFI incorporation application and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop, Companies Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum and Articles, bank capital certificate, name approval, and prescribed GAFI forms through the One-Stop Shop; pay the required Egyptian pound fees; GAFI issues the electronic incorporation approval, assigns a commercial registration number, and provides the founders with the initial Commercial Registry Extract; the incorporation is complete upon GAFI registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank certificate evidencing paid-up capital
GAFI name approval certificate
Passport or national ID copies of all founders
Registered office lease or title deed
Power of attorney for the authorized representative
First Board Resolution appointing officers and adopting statutory addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Review the GAFI electronic deficiency notice, supply the missing or corrected documents within 10 working days, and re-upload the remedial package; if GAFI raises legal interpretation issues, file a formal administrative objection with the GAFI Legal Department and request a dedicated single-case manager for accelerated review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification and social insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete ETA tax registration on Form 1 for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and payroll tax; obtain the tax card and tax identification number; file VAT registration within 30 days of exceeding the VAT threshold or immediately if voluntarily electing to register; enroll all employees and directors in NOSI and obtain the social insurance number for the company and each insured person.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate and extract
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease agreement
Board resolution appointing the legal representative and tax agent
Founder and director passport or national ID copies
Prior tax ID information for founders and directors, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA application is suspended for missing documents, submit the outstanding documents through the ETA electronic window; for social insurance discrepancies, apply to NOSI for rectification of employee data; both registrations may be escalated to the central departments under the Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical office licensing, civil defense clearance and environmental registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Governorate Premises Licensing Committee; Civil Defense Authority (Ministry of Interior); Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an offshore software development center, no industrial manufacturing license is required; however, the office premises must obtain a local operating license (Rukhsat Tashghil) and a Civil Defense fire safety certificate. File an EEAA registration/self-assessment because the activity is a commercial and information technology service with negligible environmental impact; maintain workplace health and safety compliance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry extract
Lease contract or title deed for the office premises
Civil Defense fire safety test report and certificate
Architectural and structural safety certificate for the building
Workplace health and safety plan and insurance policy
EEAA registration application and compliance self-assessment for low-risk service activity
Board resolution assigning the responsible officer for health, safety and environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the governorate license is denied or returned with comments, correct the premises deficiencies (e.g., fire extinguishers, emergency exits, ventilation) and request re-inspection; file a written appeal to the Governorate Licensing Committee within 30 days; if EEAA re-classifies the activity, submit the required mitigation measures and updated waste management plan for approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Licensing Directorate; Local Governorate Licensing Committee
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Premises Operating License (Rukhsat Tashghil Al-Mahal) and Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: List C / Category 3 – Registration and self-assessment only; full EIA report is not required for low-risk software engineering and information technology services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point source emissions; domestic wastewater and potable water standards under Law No. 4 of 1994 and Ministerial Decree No. 92 of 2013; electronic waste must be handed over to Ministry of Environment licensed recyclers under Decree No. 204 of 2021; office noise and generator exhaust must comply with the limits specified in the EEAA code of practice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Civil Defense Authority under Law No. 135 of 1981; structural load inspection certificate in accordance with the Egyptian Code for Design and Construction; workplace safety authorization and health and safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 and its executive regulations, including first-aid facilities, emergency exits, and occupational risk assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) of the Ministry of Finance, headquartered at 1 Ramsis Street, Nasr City, Cairo; official digital portals: https://www.eta.gov.eg (ETA corporate portal), https://www.elmoysr.gov.eg (unified taxpayer services portal), and https://invoice.eta.gov.eg (e-invoicing/e-receipt platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the LLC through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) One-Stop-Shop or the local Commercial Registry and obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate stating ISIC 6202 activity. Step 2: File the unified corporate registration application (Form 1) with the ETA, attaching the authenticated Articles of Association, commercial registry extract, lease contract or title deed for the registered office, board/manager resolution appointing the tax representative, and passport copies of all managers and ultimate shareholders; non-resident shareholders require no minimum capital and may own 100% of the LLC. Step 3: Obtain the electronic Tax Card and the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN), which concurrently covers income tax, VAT, payroll tax, and stamp duty withholding obligations. Step 4: Register for VAT under the same TIN either mandatorily (annual taxable supplies exceeding EGP 500,000) or voluntarily (turnover above EGP 50,000) so as to lawfully zero-rate export services; export registration is also recorded in the ETA exporter register and the National Single Window for Foreign Trade (NAFEZA) with the ACID customs pre-registration. Step 5: For cross-border service billing, open a designated foreign-currency bank account in Egypt in the name of the LLC and register the account with the Central Bank of Egypt correspondent bank for incoming SWIFT credits. ETA processing generally completes within 10 to 30 working days when acts through a licensed tax agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt is a unitary civil-law jurisdiction with no US-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections: (a) approval of a non-calendar fiscal year for corporate income tax purposes under Article 34 of Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 30/2023; (b) the simplified presumptive tax regime for small businesses under Law 152/2020 (annual turnover not exceeding EGP 3 million, as amended), electively replacing standard corporate tax, VAT filing, and payroll administration with turnover-based taxation at graduated rates of 0.5% to 5%; (c) start-up tax exemptions and securities/options deferral elections under Law 30/2023 subject to ETA eligibility certification; (d) definitive election to zero-rate export services under Article 8(2) of the VAT Law and the Executive Regulations upon producing foreign-currency repatriation evidence; and (e) no group/consolidated filing election exists, meaning the LLC is taxed as a stand-alone entity; hybrid-mismatch protection relies on domestic general anti-abuse rules under Articles 60-63 of Law 91/2005 and Egyptian tax treaty applicable provisions, not on an elective instrument.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (VAT Law 67/2016, Article 15); voluntary registration is available from EGP 50,000 of annual taxable supplies (Executive Regulations, Article 26). An ODC exporting software services is effectively obliged to register regardless of turnover in order to claim the 0% export rate and issue compliant e-invoices with ETA clearance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is fully mandatory for all VAT registrants in Egypt. Every B2B/B2G invoice must be submitted in structured XML through the ETA Data Exchange Protocol (DXP) using a REST API, SFTP, or the ETA web portal, and the invoice is legally issued only upon real-time ETA validation and stamping (synchronization). Non-integrated paper invoices are invalid for VAT deduction and trigger a fine of EGP 50,000 per invoice (Article 74 of Law 67/2016 as amended). The parallel e-receipt mandate covers B2C transactions. ERP systems must be certified or the taxpayer must use the ETA portal; corrective credit/debit notes are also subject to the same clearance workflow.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying services are taxed at 0% under Articles 8 and 9 of VAT Law 67/2016. For ODC software engineering, development, and maintenance services supplied by the Egyptian LLC to a non-resident group company or foreign client, the following cumulative conditions apply: (i) the recipient must be resident outside Egypt and possess no taxable establishment in Egypt for this service; (ii) the commercial and economic benefit of the service is realized entirely outside Egypt; (iii) the consideration is invoiced in foreign currency and settled through Egyptian banks; (iv) the foreign-currency proceeds are repatriated to Egypt within the applicable Central Bank of Egypt deadline; and (v) the taxpayer retains contemporaneous contracts, delivery and acceptance evidence (e.g., technical sign-offs, time sheets, repository handover logs) proving that the software services were rendered from the Egyptian ODC to the offshore recipient. The ETA applies the substance-over-form principle; mere outsourcing labels without staffing, execution, and risk infrastructure will be recharacterized as a domestic service taxable at 14%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration bearing the ACID code (applicable to software distribution on physical media only)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export (where applicable)
Commercial invoice in USD/EUR referencing the ODC master service agreement
Old and new: signed ODC/software development service agreement with non-resident counterparty
Foreign-currency inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice from the non-resident payer
Delivery and acceptance certificate, technical milestone report, or repository handover evidence signed by the offshore client
Time-and-effort or cost-plus reconciliation report for intra-group centralized services
Currency repatriation compliance certificate issued by the designated Egyptian bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA conducts strict post-clearance audits of zero-rating claims. Unsubstantiated or fraudulent export zero-rating results in: reassessment at the standard 14% VAT rate; monthly late-payment interest at 2% of the tax due (Article 77 of Law 67/2016 as amended); per-invoice fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 for false or non-electronic invoices; retrospective clawback of any VAT refunds or input-tax recoveries; and criminal sanctions under Articles 70-75 of Law 67/2016 for tax evasion and invoice forgery, including imprisonment and fines of up to double the evaded tax. The ETA's period of assessment is generally five years, extended in cases of deliberate concealment, and the Large Taxpayer Center and Export Recovery Unit may suspend refund cycles and impose immediate withholding offsets when documentation is incomplete.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — البنك المركزي المصري, operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), with exclusive jurisdiction over exchange control, authorized-bank licensing, and FX market supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Post-March 2024 exchange-rate unification under the CBE–IMF program, the Egyptian pound (EGP) trades in a single free-float band; current-account transactions (service receipts/payments) are fully convertible upon documentary compliance with CBE anti-money-laundering and repatriation rules. Capital-account transactions (equity injections, inbound loans, dividends) remain subject to a documentary gate administered by CBE-authorized banks: no pre-approval is required for equity capital contributions, but profit and dividend remittances require (i) audited financial statements, (ii) an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax clearance certificate, (iii) proof of dividend withholding tax (standard 10%), and (iv) a beneficial-ownership declaration. Practical remittance hurdles are substantially reduced post-float; banks may quote wider spreads during periods of excess volatility, but no formal FX rationing or multiple-rate regime is in force.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory export-proceeds surrender regime (100% under February-2017 CBE directives, subsequently 50% in 2023) was terminated upon the March-2024 unified-float reforms. There is currently no statutory conversion ratio: exporters and service suppliers may retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in a CBE-authorized foreign-currency account or convert at the free market rate. The controlling obligation is repatriation: proceeds from software/IT services (ISIC 6202) must be collected through an authorized Egyptian bank within 90 days from the date of service rendition or invoice maturity, whichever is earlier; each export invoice must be matched to a CBE banking receipt to satisfy both exchange-control and ETA transfer-pricing review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + USD/EGP Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account + USD/EGP Operational Account
USD/EGP Operational Account + FX Hedging Line
USD/EGP Operational Account + Cross-Border Clearing Concentrator

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low as a stand-alone primary clearing rail; Medium strictly as an ancillary settlement layer. Legal constraints: Wise B2B, Payoneer, and similar EMBs/EMIs hold no CBE banking license and cannot receive statutory export proceeds for Egyptian legal entities under CBE Law 194/2020, which mandates that all export/service proceeds be repatriated via an authorized Egyptian bank within 90 days. Acceptable deployment: supplementary collection of small-ticket client fees (e.g., sub-USD 10,000 per transaction and ideally under 5% of annual revenue), with each transaction fully recorded, resolved onward, and mirrored by an equivalent inward credit to the Egyptian anchor account on a monthly basis.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance in Egypt by at least one authorized signatory—normally the local resident general manager—for biometric verification and wet-ink signature capture at the branch; this cannot be substituted by notarization alone. Non-resident shareholders/directors may open accounts only through a Power of Attorney (POA) notarized abroad and legalized by the relevant Egyptian consulate, with the resident signatory present for the interview. Fully remote video onboarding is not available for newly incorporated Egyptian LLCs; video verification is accepted only as a supplementary step for pre-existing premium bank clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intra-group revenue concentration: single offshore parent/client contracting the entire ODC output, raising transfer-pricing and lack-of-commercial-substance concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive group organizational chart; executed MSA/SOW demonstrating real service delivery; functional analysis showing the Egyptian LLC as a routine low-risk developer hub with no ownership of high-value IP or DEMPE functions; arm's-length transfer-pricing study filed in Egyptian Form 3-1; and projected P&L demonstrating a routine-cost-plus remuneration profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder with an opaque source-of-funds trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized board/subscription resolution for the capital contribution; certified commercial-registry extract showing the updated capital structure; 3-6 months bank statements of the remitting shareholder; source-of-wealth declaration signed by each UBO; CBE direct-investment registration form submitted via the receiving authorized bank; SWIFT MT103 remittance advice labeled 'Equity Capital Contribution'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-currency inflows arriving irregularly via Wise/Payoneer rather than through the authorized-bank channel, creating CBE reporting gaps.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written rationale for ancillary-rail usage; itemized receipts ledger mapping every EMI payout to an underlying client invoice; executed client agreements; quarterly reconciliation statements submitted to the relationship manager; and a signed undertaking that 100% of EMI inflows will be formally repatriated to the Egyptian anchor account within the statutory 90-day window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) opacity, nominee shareholder arrangements, or undisclosed indirect ownership of the Egyptian LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified up-to-date shareholders' register; statutory UBO declarations under Egypt's AML Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) and its executive regulations; commercial-registry extract reflecting every shareholder and manager; passport copies and tax-residence certificates of all natural-person UBOs; and a nil-sanctions screening letter from a reputable compliance provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 from the subscribing shareholder's overseas bank to the LLC's designated capital-collection account (Capital Escrow sub-account) at an authorized Egyptian bank, labeled with CBE statistical purpose code 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (code category 320). The receiving bank files the CBE direct-investment registration and issues a Foreign Investment Certificate; funds may remain in USD or be converted into EGP at the free market rate. Required attachments on first draw: certified articles of association, latest commercial-registry extract, tax-card and VAT registration certificates, notarized subscription resolution, and 3-6 months source-of-funds statements from the remitting shareholder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for software-engineering service settlements is SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic wire transfers (operational expenses, subcontractor fees, management fees, dividends, and tax payments); SWIFT MT202 is used for interbank cover in currency liquidity chains. Commercial Letters of Credit (usance/sight) are confined to physical-hardware imports (e.g., servers, workstations) on a standby or documentary basis. Outbound disbursements require the underlying agreement, vendor invoice, and proof of WHT collection (10% standard Egyptian WHT on services/dividends to non-resident payees, subject to DTT relief demonstrated via a certificate of tax residence); dividend wires additionally require audited financial statements and a valid ETA tax clearance certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP FX Forwards (tenor 1-12 months) from CBE-authorized banks, requiring an underlying trade invoice, service contract, or procurement commitment.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on the EGP, permitted post-2024 liberalization for corporate and non-resident counterparties hedging EGP exposure without settling principal.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) with major Egyptian and international banks for longer-tenor exposures covering capex or recurring receivables.
FX options (limited availability on request from largest authorized dealers) for premium-based hedging of adverse EGP moves.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end (if fiscal year = Dec 31, due April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 1,000–5,000 escalating per month; interest on unpaid tax; risk of administrative strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Annual Renewal and Annual Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) / Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from anniversary of commercial registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalty of EGP 200 per month capped at EGP 2,000; administrative suspension of commercial registration after 6 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Annual Confirmation Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) – Corporate Compliance Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, no later than June 30 for calendar-year entities (or within 30 days of anniversary if different reference date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EGP 10,000 to EGP 100,000 for non-disclosure; additional daily penalty for continued breach; potential freezing of corporate actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All LLCs, irrespective of size, must appoint at least one certified external auditor; mandatory for tax filing and regulatory solvency evidence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) – substantially converged with IFRS; IFRS permitted for consolidated or listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually confirm all shareholders holding >25% and any natural person exercising ultimate control; file updated register with GAFI, obtain receipt of acknowledgment; reported ownership changes trigger intermediate filings within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assemblies and Board Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% under Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 for commercial, industrial, and IT service entities
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for a standard Egyptian LLC. Preferential deductions are available: 30%–50% deduction of qualifying investment costs in underdeveloped governorates, accelerated depreciation on machinery and technology assets, and utilization of prior-year tax losses within the 5-year carryforward window. Software export and offshore development center models do not receive a blanket exemption, but treaty relief may lower outbound withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT Legal Persons Return) submitted electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at www.incometax.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; quarterly provisional tax instalments for estimated corporate income tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is no later than 4 months after the end of the fiscal/accounting year; for a calendar-year LLC, the return is due by April 30 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross operating revenue from software development, maintenance, technical support, and related outsourcing services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide revenue; foreign-source software services must be separately declared to support foreign tax credit claims and treaty allocation principles

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cost of revenue, including software engineer payroll, subcontractor fees, data center costs, and license costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any recharge from a non-resident related party must be supported by an arm's length TP analysis; attach contemporaneous benchmarking or draft local file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative expenses, rent, utilities, professional fees, and non-resident related-party service charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For management fees and technical service fees paid abroad, provide valid invoices, beneficial ownership certificates, and TP documentation to avoid disallowance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit before tax computed under Egyptian GAAP with audited independent financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should confirm transfer pricing policy does not shift profit outside Egypt; no additional return required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses, fines, provisions, and statutory depreciation adjustments; deduction of investment incentives and tax-exempt income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIT is entity-level; foreign owners do not directly fill this box but must provide documentation of actual transactions for ETA audit review

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unabsorbed tax losses from previous years deducted against current-year taxable profits, subject to the 5-year statutory limit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is available only if the Egyptian entity has substantiated Malaysian-like filing of prior losses and continues to satisfy ETA milestone evidence requirements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All adjustments summarized: net profit less adjusted costs and deductions, reduced by carryforward losses, producing final taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reflect arm's length profit margin typical for an offshore development center under the selected TP methodology

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed on Box 7 taxable income using the statutory rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax clearance or non-resident signature is required; this position is the resident LLC's statutory liability

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly provisional CIT payments, tax credits, and foreign tax credits for eligible foreign-paid taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident withholding taxes deducted from the LLC's payments abroad are not creditable unless the LLC is economically the taxpayer of record under Egyptian tax law

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due after offsetting prepayments and credits; overpayments generate refund claims reviewed by the ETA
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors remain jointly liable for unpaid balance; foreign parent guarantee or escrow may be required if profits are repatriated before final clearance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic monthly surcharge of 2% of the outstanding tax for each month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the due tax, plus administrative fines of up to EGP 30,000. Intentional failure to file can invoke criminal fines and imprisonment provisions of Law 91/2005.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% domestic withholding tax on cash dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; treaty protection may reduce this to 5% under applicable Double Taxation Agreements
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the competent tax authority of its state of residence, certified and legalized, and submit an Egyptian DTA relief application to the ETA before or within the WHT filing window. The Egyptian paying company must retain the TRC and beneficial ownership declaration on file to record the reduced rate at source; otherwise the excess WHT can be reclaimed only through the annual tax return process after the withholding has been remitted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic final withholding tax on cross-border software royalties, license fees, and debt interest paid by the LLC to non-residents is 20%. Treaty relief commonly caps interest at 10%–15% and royalties at 10%–15%, subject to Turkish-style economic substance and beneficial ownership tests on the recipient.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million aggregate value of controlled transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File obligation arises when the consolidated global group revenue exceeds EGP 200 million; Country-by-Country Reporting applies above EGP 20 billion consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not administer GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) licensing; nevertheless, the ETA enforces a de facto economic substance standard through anti-avoidance, tax residency, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse rules. A non-resident-controlled LLC operating as an offshore development center must evidence physical office, payroll, decision-making, disposition over contracts, and genuine operational risk to sustain treaty claims and avoid recharacterization as a shell entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully understating software deployment revenue, issuing false invoices to foreign parent companies, artificially inflating input costs, omitting related-party commissions, or concealing bank assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine equal to the evaded tax amount, in addition to automatic surcharges. ETA may impose the higher of the evaded tax plus 100% or 2% monthly delinquency, as well as asset seizure and blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve falsified accounts are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and heavy financial penalties; applicable measures include freezing of personal assets, a blanket travel ban issued by the prosecutor, and criminal incarceration of the designated responsible officer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length management fees, using captive software R&D contracts with no risk assumption, failing to prepare Local File within statutory deadlines, or omitting the annual TP disclosure annex
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA authorized TP adjustment with deemed profit recomputation, underpayment penalty of 30% of additional assessed tax, and denial of deductions. Interest accrues monthly from the original filing date; repeated violations raise the penalty to 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who implemented intercompany pricing with no documented policy are personally liable for resulting tax assessment shortfall in the course of winding up or asset stripping; they may also face travel restrictions during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding the LLC formally legitimate but operating with no physical office in Egypt, no IT assets, no engineering payroll beyond minimal staff, and everything performed via sub-contractors abroad, used mainly to route profits artificially
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, retroactive withholding tax on repatriated profits, disallowance of claimed exempt or reduced-rate treatment, and full re-audit liability. The ETA can reclassify the entity as a controlled foreign activity and treat its entire revenue as subject to income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally ordered to return distributed profits and pay the differential tax plus interest if the corporate veil is pierced; criminal referral follows when the sham structure was used to evade tax and the directors failed to maintain substantive records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register ultimate beneficial owners in Egypt’s automated compliance registers, concealment of foreign shareholders receiving repatriated dividends, or conducting excessive cross-border cash transfers without disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines starting at EGP 50,000 and escalating to EGP 1,000,000, with director disqualification and suspension of electronic filing accounts; fines double for repeated noncompliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal liability attaches to the amir of the board and money laundering compliance officer; sanctions include disqualification from serving as a director in Egypt, personal fines, and in cases of intentional concealment, imprisonment for up to 3 years.
